text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet starts next week discussions on the 1997 budget law, with a three percent rise on its current level.
- King departs to London on Thursday on a private two week visit.
- Electricity company workers stage strike on Wednesday.
- King Hussein and Queen Noor inaugurate four national projects, part of the kingdom's celebrations of the king's birthday.
- Crown Prince Hassan emphasises the need to liberalise the economy and placing "it in a situation that allows it to breathe".
- Finance minister says no new jobs in the coming 1997 budget.
- Jordanian-Pakistani economic talks start in the chamber of commerce.
- King Hussein urges completion of laws to revive the economy.
- Crown Prince says no alternative to the (IMF-directed) economic restructuring programme because "it is our admission on the map of the world economy".
- Justice minister says the first batch of pardonned detainees to be announced on Saturday.
